rows.summary: All three sub-claims hold on main: renewals share the (default 10) task-store pool with a 30 s acquire wait against a 15 s TTL, the renewer shares the executors' runtime, and an executor cut off from the database runs on unfenced until a renewal succeeds. rows.probe: Two replicas of scripts/live/replica (NAME/PORT/DATABASE_URL as partition_live.py), each through its own toxiproxy link (pg_a 15432, pg_b 15433). (1) Starvation: build the replica with PostgresTaskStore::new_with_pool_size(url, 3); on N1 park 300 tasks ('park') and open SubscribeToTask on each against N1; send 'hold' to N1 (returnImmediately); every 2 s send a continuation of it to N2. Decides: an N1 log line 'turn claims not renewed', then the hold task stored TASK_STATE_FAILED with the reaper's text ('the replica running this task stopped before it finished') or N2 admitting the continuation while N1's executor is alive. (2) Partition: a 'tick'-like executor that POSTs a counter to a local webhook every 500 ms; disable pg_a 20 s; count POSTs from N1 after the task was ended or taken over (any > 0 = duplicated side effects).
rows.replica_failure: Normal load: nothing. Pool pressure (hundreds of idle subscribers per pod, E-F25), a lock queue (E-F11) or a CPU-bound executor on the runtime: renewals miss a TTL, and a quiet turn (a long model call) is ended failed/transient by a reaper while its pod is healthy. A pod partitioned from PostgreSQL keeps calling the model, tools and child agents for the whole partition; the client re-sends the transient failure elsewhere, so side effects run twice.
rows.production_refuse: No: Production cannot see pool settings or executor behaviour; fix in code.

rows.summary: One optimistic append point per tenant chain for the whole fleet: each append is at least 2 round trips and every success invalidates the other replicas' reads. Back of the envelope (conjecture, not measured): with N saturated contenders a request loses 8 rounds with probability about ((N-1)/N)^8, 0.4% at N=2, 3.9% at N=3, 17% at N=5. So failures may appear well below the report's N >= 9, and under require_record(true) (Auditable) those requests are refused.
rows.remaining: A decision on the append protocol; then thresholds measured (X17).
rows.probe: Report X17: 1, 2, 3 and 5 replicas with AuditLog over PostgresAuditStore and require_record(true), load at 200-500 rps through a round-robin balancer; count 'audit append lost the race' errors and refused requests, and audited appends/s. Decides the thresholds; the mechanism is settled by reading.
rows.options: (a) Append in one transaction under pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('a2a.audit:'||chain,0)): read head, insert, commit. No lost races and the same single-chain order; throughput stays bounded by one transaction per append per chain. S-M, no format change. (b) Per-replica sub-chains with periodic cross-signed checkpoints: scales, but changes the chain model, export and verification. L. (c) Jittered backoff and more attempts: XS, a mitigation only. Also take time_ms from the database in (a). Recommendation: (a).
rows.replica_failure: With auditing on PostgreSQL and require_record(true), under sustained load on 3-5 pods a few percent of audited calls fail 'audit append lost the race' and are refused; adding pods adds contention, not audited throughput.

rows.probe: Two processes, N1 (7811) via pg_a with no toxic and N2 (7812) via pg_b with a 300 ms latency toxic (POST /proxies/pg_b/toxics {"type":"latency","attributes":{"latency":300},"stream":"downstream"}), which widens the window to more than 0.5 s. 1) 'hold' to N1 with returnImmediately, task T. 2) Build a continuation M of T with metadata {"a2a-rust.com/idempotency-key":"<uuid>"} and returnImmediately. 3) Send M to N2 in a thread; poll psql SELECT 1 FROM idempotency_keys WHERE key='<uuid>' every 20 ms; the moment the row appears, send the identical M to N1. Decides: N1 answers a Task (no error) whose history lacks M's messageId; N2 answers 'already being processed' about 5 s later; tasks.data->'history' never gains M and no replica logs a run of M. new_findings.where: src/handler/claims/reaper/mod.rs:89-131 (look/end), src/store/claim/postgres.rs:52-57 (ABANDONED_PLAIN_SQL), src/handler/claims/mod.rs:389-396 (renewal error path), src/store/pg_retry.rs:139-153 (no acquire_timeout)
new_findings.finding: A database outage or failover longer than the claim TTL (15 s) lets the reapers end LIVE turns. During the outage no claim is renewed, so every claim expires on the database clock and every quiet turn's row is older than a TTL. When the database returns, each replica's pending or next reaper look (every TTL), including the owner's own (end() never checks claims.held), races the owners' renewals, which are themselves stuck in sqlx acquire/connect backoff. A reaper that wins claims the task, stores failed/transient with 'the replica running this task stopped before it finished', pushes it, and the owner then cancels its executor ('taken over'). The renewal UPDATE does not check expiry, so an owner that renews first keeps its claim; the outcome is a race.
new_findings.scenario: Kubernetes on a managed PostgreSQL (RDS/Cloud SQL HA failover typically takes 20-120 s), 2-5 pods: after a failover, in-flight turns waiting on a model (no events to write) are ended failed/transient although every pod stayed up; clients re-send, so side effects run twice. Single pod: the pod's own reaper can end its own turn. The book's 'Restart PostgreSQL mid-turn: the turn went on writing' was measured before the reaper and with a short restart. Probe: partition_live.py setup; 'hold' on N1; disable both pg_a and pg_b for 25 s, re-enable; repeat 10 times and count tasks stored TASK_STATE_FAILED with the reaper's text while N1 logs 'hold ended, cancelled=true'.

new_findings.finding: A cancel taken by a replica not running the task appends nothing to the task's event log (throwaway writer, then save_status_delta only), so the log, and with the audit feature the chain's task.event records, never hold the Canceled ending. If the owner's executor writes once more after the cancel, that non-terminal event is appended (APPEND_SQL is fenced by the claim token only, not by terminal state, and non-terminal events are logged before the fold) and only then refused by the save. The log then ends on an event the stored task does not have, and supersede records the Canceled verdict only when the refused event was terminal. Same-replica cancels and the reaper (fixed for N-E-2) do log their ending.
new_findings.scenario: Audit export of a task cancelled through the balancer (N-1 of N cancels) shows no terminal task.event, and may show an artifact chunk recorded after the cancel; a log consumer replaying task_events never sees the task end.
